review_scope: Complete enterprise57-line and organization45-line custom-model procedures, four complete BYOK reusables and complete five-line feature file read;71 parser occurrences reviewed. One operative supported-feature variable line reviewed without a full variable receipt. Preview/role/enterprise prerequisite, access-grant, credential/provider/deployment and client boundaries retained. No key changes, costs, native activation, policy adoption or rights clearance.

claims.statement: Enterprise custom models use customer LLM API keys under the copilot-byok feature declaration; this is separate from ordinary GitHub-hosted model selection.
Shared BYOK introduction and rationale define provider/preview/governance context, not independent compliance or cost-saving proof.
Enterprise owners are addressed, with a strong recommendation for minimum necessary API-key scopes; actual owner status and key scopes are unverified.
Adding a key and selecting models makes them available only through supported BYOK features, with picker grouping under the enterprise name; no inference about all Copilot surfaces.
Enterprise navigation, AI controls and Configure custom models precede shared key-addition procedure; no credentials or settings are changed here.
Enterprise model availability is configurable for organizations through Added models and Configure/All organizations/X organizations; displayed organization count is not observed by source review.
The Access tab is available only when the model is Enabled; opening configuration is not enabling access.
Enterprise access can allow all organizations or select organizations individually; choosing all is a distinct broad grant, not default assumption.
Saving availability is a mutation; organization, chat and surface links remain separate dependencies, not runtime enforcement.
Organization custom models use customer keys under copilot-byok scope, independently from personal local-client BYOK.
Organization-owner governance/data-security/compliance goals are rationale, not certification or verified permission.
An enterprise owner must enable Enable custom models before organization setup; the organization's procedure cannot override that prerequisite.
Organization key configuration strongly recommends minimum necessary scopes; no real key is collected or exposed in review.
Organization-added models are described as available to members through supported BYOK features and grouped under organization name; membership does not prove every client supports BYOK.
Organization settings and Copilot Models/Custom models navigation lead to shared key addition; previously reviewed navigation dependencies are not duplicate full receipts.
Enterprise setup, chat and supported-surfaces links are references; account grant and surface applicability need separate reconciliation.
BYOK adds custom models to an enterprise or organization using customer keys and a supported-feature variable; the preview note is nested and retained separately.
Fine-tuned models are supported but function/quality varies with fine-tuning; the source recommends testing and careful output review before production.
Personal locally configured LLM keys are a separate feature linked by the introduction; enterprise credentials are not automatically personal-client credentials.
Choosing providers that meet organization/regulatory requirements is a governance rationale, not automatic compliance or rights clearance.
Existing payment methods/contracts/credits/rates and avoiding overages are stated cost-management goals, not verified billing caps.
Model access control and provider-dashboard usage/billing visibility are rationale; actual monitoring and access settings remain unverified.
Existing custom/specialized-model flexibility is an intended capability, not universal model compatibility.
Shared addition selects provider, names the key for picker display and enters the API key; these are credential-bearing operations not performed by ingestion.
OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI use key-associated model fetching followed by selection; the source does not claim this same discovery mechanism for every listed provider.
Microsoft Foundry requires a deployment URL plus manually entered Model ID; provider-specific deployment identity cannot be omitted.
Models with different Foundry deployment URLs cannot share the same added API key entry; create separate key entries per deployment URL.
Setup image paths and alt text were read as evidence, not visual image review or per-image redistribution clearance.
Saving selected/added models completes the documented configuration action, not verified model inference behavior.
BYOK is public preview and subject to change at the pin.
The feature file identifies Copilot BYOK, not Copilot Models, and enables fpt/ghec versions only; generic navigation includes do not widen it to GHES.
The pinned supported-feature variable resolves to Copilot Chat, Copilot CLI and IDEs; this targeted variable review does not mark the full variable artifact reviewed.
The pinned BYOK provider list includes Anthropic; provider membership is not model-specific compatibility, current entitlement, key permission or policy clearance.
